note: [MS-XCA] 2.5 (the Windows NTFS compression format, RtlDecompressBuffer), written from the specification; no parameters, as in CyberChef. The chunk loop is a private primitive (an FL prototype cost 12 to 49 VM steps per output byte). Added: corrupt data is E_COERCE naming the fault (bad chunk signature, a chunk or word cut short, a match before the start of its chunk, a chunk that expands past 4096 bytes), and output past the value limit stops with E_LIMIT_VALUE. A zero header ends the data and bytes after it are ignored; empty input is empty output. Compression is not offered (CyberChef has none). Cross-checked: the streams of the test encoder (with and without the end marker, stored and compressed chunks, 70 inputs of 0 to 256 KiB) decode the same here and in CyberChef, and 400 damaged streams (cut or with changed bytes) are rejected or decoded identically by both. Where they differ CyberChef is wrong: it takes a chunk header whose size field is 0 (a chunk of exactly one byte, which a 4097-byte input ends with) for the end marker and drops that chunk, while this treats only a zero header as the end.

[MS-XCA] 2.3 and 2.4, Plain LZ77, written from the specification (the worked examples of section 3.1 are tests); no parameters. The decoder is a private primitive. Added: truncated data, a match before the start of the output and a bad long-length field are E_COERCE naming the fault, and output past the value limit stops with E_LIMIT_VALUE (a 32-bit match length allocates nothing). Empty input is E_COERCE because the stream starts with a flag word. Compression is not offered. Cross-checked: the streams of the test encoder (70 inputs of 0 to 256 KiB, including 32-bit match lengths) decode identically here and in CyberChef, and 400 damaged streams are rejected or decoded identically by both.

[MS-XCA] 2.1 and 2.2, LZ77+Huffman, written from the specification (the worked example of section 3.2 is a test); no parameters. The bit-level decoder is a private primitive. Blocks of 64 KiB follow one another, each with its own 256-byte table; the end-of-data symbol (256 with all input read) or a final 64 KiB block ends the data. Added: an over-subscribed or incomplete Huffman table, truncated data, a match before the start of the output and a bad long-length field are E_COERCE naming the fault, and output past the value limit stops with E_LIMIT_VALUE. Empty input is E_COERCE. Compression is not offered. Cross-checked: CyberChef takes the decompressed size as a parameter (4096 by default) and reads one block only; this finds the end itself and reads any number of 64 KiB blocks, each with its own table, as [MS-XCA] 2.2 describes (CyberChef fails on every stream of more than one block). For one block, CyberChef decodes most of the test encoder's streams but not all: it refills its bit buffer when fewer than 15 bits remain, this decoder when fewer than 16 remain (as the pseudo-code of the specification and Samba's lzxpress_huffman.c, read and not run), and the two read a following length byte from different places, so six of 57 single-block streams fail in CyberChef (match offset out of range or truncated bit stream). The symbol 256 ends the data here when all input has been read, CyberChef ends when the declared size is reached; a stream whose last symbols hold a real match of length 3 at distance 1 (also symbol 256) in the final 32 bits is therefore read short here, a case the test encoder avoids and no Windows encoder is known to produce. Bytes after the last block are E_COERCE here (no size to stop at), ignored by CyberChef.
